To cover a room floor with the largest possible identical square tiles without cutting, the side length of the tile must equal:
Define Highest Common Factor (HCF) or Greatest Common Divisor (GCD).
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The HCF (or GCD) of two or more numbers is the largest positive integer that divides each of the numbers completely without leaving a remainder.

questions.question_text: Find the HCF of 24, 36, and 60 by prime factorisation.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 24 = 2³×3, 36 = 2²×3², 60 = 2²×3×5. Common prime factors with lowest powers = 2² × 3¹ = 4 × 3 = 12.

questions.question_text: A hall floor measures 18 m by 24 m. Sameeksha wants to tile it with square tiles of maximum size without cutting any tile. (a) Find maximum tile side. (b) Find total number of tiles needed.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Tile side = HCF(18, 24) = 6 meters. (b) Tiles along length = 24/6 = 4. Tiles along width = 18/6 = 3. Total tiles = 4 × 3 = 12 tiles.

questions.question_text: A charity distributes 225 kg of rice and 750 kg of wheat in bags of equal weight containing either only rice or only wheat. (a) Find maximum weight of each bag. (b) How many bags of rice and wheat are created?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Maximum weight = HCF(225, 750). 225 = 3²×5², 750 = 2×3×5³. HCF = 3¹×5² = 75 kg. (b) Rice bags = 225/75 = 3 bags. Wheat bags = 750/75 = 10 bags. Total = 13 bags.

Three traffic signals change color every 12 seconds, 18 seconds, and 24 seconds respectively. If they all change simultaneously at 9:00 AM, at what time will they change together next?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Find LCM(12, 18, 24). 12 = 2²×3, 18 = 2×3², 24 = 2³×3. LCM = 2³ × 3² = 8 × 9 = 72 seconds = 1 min 12 sec. Next simultaneous change = 9:01:12 AM.

questions.question_text: Three bells toll together at intervals of 9, 12, and 15 minutes. (a) Calculate LCM(9, 12, 15). (b) Convert time to hours. (c) If they toll at 6:00 AM, when will they toll together next?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) 9 = 3², 12 = 2²×3, 15 = 3×5. LCM = 2²×3²×5 = 180 minutes. (b) 180 / 60 = 3 hours. (c) Next toll time = 6:00 AM + 3 hours = 9:00 AM.

Write the prime factorisations of 45 and 36, and find their HCF.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 45 = 3² × 5; 36 = 2² × 3². Common prime factor is 3 with lowest power 3². HCF = 9.

questions.question_text: Write the prime factorisations of 45 and 36, and find their LCM.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 45 = 3² × 5; 36 = 2² × 3². All prime factors with max powers: 2², 3², 5¹. LCM = 4 × 9 × 5 = 180.

questions.question_text: Express 144, 180, and 192 as products of prime factors. Calculate both HCF(144, 180, 192) and LCM(144, 180, 192).

A school sports coordinator wants to arrange 108 boys and 144 girls into equal rows containing either only boys or only girls. (a) Find maximum number of students per row. (b) Find total number of rows formed.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Max per row = HCF(108, 144). 108 = 2²×3³, 144 = 2⁴×3². HCF = 2²×3² = 36 students per row. (b) Boys rows = 108/36 = 3. Girls rows = 144/36 = 4. Total rows = 7.

State the formula relating HCF, LCM, and two numbers 'a' and 'b'. Does this formula hold for three numbers?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Formula: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b. No, this formula does NOT hold for three numbers.

questions.question_text: The HCF of two co-prime numbers is 1 and their LCM is 66. Find two possible pairs of numbers.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Since HCF = 1, a × b = 66. Co-prime factor pairs of 66: (1, 66), (2, 33), (3, 22), (6, 11). Any two pairs are valid.

questions.question_text: The product of two numbers is 2160 and their HCF is 12. (a) Find their LCM. (b) If one number is 60, find the other number. (c) Verify that HCF × LCM = Product.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) LCM = 2160 / 12 = 180. (b) Other number = 2160 / 60 = 36. (c) HCF × LCM = 12 × 180 = 2160 = Product verified.

Can two numbers have 15 as their HCF and 110 as their LCM? Give reasons.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: No, because the HCF must always divide the LCM completely. 110 is not divisible by 15 (110 ÷ 15 = 7.33).

A sweet seller has 420 kaju barfis and 130 badam barfis. She wants to stack them in equal counts such that they take up minimum tray space. (a) Find maximum number of barfis per stack. (b) Find number of stacks for each type.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Stack count = HCF(420, 130) = 10 barfis per stack. (b) Kaju stacks = 420/10 = 42; Badam stacks = 130/10 = 13 stacks.
